q: Define Economics in the words of Professor Robbins and explain the subject matter of Economics?
a: Answers: Professor Robbins’ Definition of Economics: "Economics studies human behavior as a relationship between ends and scarce means which have alternative uses." Subject Matter of Economics: Professor Lionel Robbins is of the opinion that the purpose of Economic motive is to satisfy unlimited human wants by limited means. He further proposes that man should follow a certain line of action to satisfy his unlimited wants by his scarce means. Thus, preferring and satisfying the most important want first, he can be able to solve many of his economic problems gradually. Thus, to seek the solution to the economic problem; following a certain line of action, is the subject matter of Economics, according to Robbins. This definition is based on the fact that (a) the ends (wants) are unlimited. (b) The means (resources) to achieve these ends, are limited, (c) these means are capable of alternative uses, and (d) a line of action should be followed to attain the immediate wants. E.g. A sick child wants toys but his parents can either buy medicines or toys with a limited amount of money.

q: Describe the subject matter of Economics in the light of the definition of Professor Alfred Marshall?
a: Answers: Professor Marshall’s Definition of Economics: “Economics is a study of mankind in the ordinary business of life: it enquires how he gets his income and how he uses it. Thus it is on one side a study of wealth and on the other, and more important side, a part of the study of man." Subject Matter of Economics: This definition states that Economics is closely related to our ordinary business of life. It discusses our economic problems, individually, as well as, collectively. We examine, moreover, our efforts made for the material welfare and well-being of our life. In short, we can say that Economics is related to our ordinary economic problems and that how can we attain prosperity by material requisites. Professor Alfred Marshall determines the subject matter of Economics as, "The individual and collective human efforts to produce material requisites for human welfare and well-being."

q: What do you mean by wants?
a: Describe the kinds and characteristics of wants? Answers: Wants: Certain goods and services are required to meet the requisites of human life. In Economics, these requisites are called wants. Kinds of Wants: Economic Wants: These wants are satisfied by consuming goods and services, purchased for cash (money). Our economic activities are meant for earning money, with the aim to satisfy our wants. Non-Economic Wants: These wants are satisfied by free gifts of nature i.e. air, water, sunshine, etc. People can get them without any labor or payment. The love of the mother is also included in non-economic wants. Characteristics: Wants are unlimited: Human wants are uncountable wants that have no limits at all. If a man satisfies too many wants at a time, he cannot bring them to an end; because after the satisfaction of wants, they appear again to be satisfied. Wants to recur: After the satisfaction of a particular want, it occurs again and again. Similar is the case with all other wants because they are recurring by nature. Wants are competitive: Wants compete among themselves, being unlimited. Some of our wants are more important than others; while some are preferable. It makes no difference if we postpone less important wants for the human being. In this way, according to their importance and preference, wants to compete among themselves. Wants are alternatives: Many wants can be satisfied by alternative methods e.g. the want for food can be satisfied by eating rice, fruits, meat, and bread. Similarly, we may travel by bus, motorcycle, and bicycle or by train.
